sense: not the one nor the other of two

terms.grammar: pronoun and adjective; gen. neutrīus, dat. neutrī
evidence: Caes. BC 1.35.5: dēbēmus neutrum eōrum contrā alium juvāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With a genitive of the pair: neutrum eōrum, neither of them. Of more than two, “none” is nūllus (see none). “Neither … nor” is nec … nec.

phrases.latin: Leporēs duo quī īnsequitur, is neutrum capit.
phrases.english: Whoever chases two hares catches neither.

phrases.latin: Ad duo festīnāns neutrum bene perēgeris.
phrases.english: Rush at two things and you’ll finish neither well.

phrases.latin: ita fīet, ut, cum aequālī cūrā linguam utramque tuērī coeperīmus, neutra alterī officiat
phrases.english: so it will come about that, once we begin to look after both languages with equal care, neither will get in the way of the other
otherwise neither is enough without the other

phrases.latin: dēbēmus neutrum eōrum contrā alium juvāre
phrases.english: we ought to help neither of them against the other

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-publilius, loci-quintilianus), checked against the editions named there.

Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text; from N onwards that numbering differs from Meyer’s. “Ps.-Publil.” marks lines from the later collections printed with him.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
